([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2021–2022) | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2021]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2021) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship|FIBA Americas U16 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship|2019 Brazil]]|[[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Caleb Michael David Houstan''' (born January 9, 2003) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. Houstan was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. He won a silver medal with Canada at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]]. ==High school career== For his first three years, Houstan attended [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. On July 17, 2020, Houstan announced he would forgo his senior year, graduate from high school early, and reclassify to class of 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29480676/caleb-houstan-no-3-recruit-2022-reclassifies-2021 |title=Caleb Houstan, No. 3 recruit in 2022, reclassifies to 2021 |website=ESPN.com |first=Jonathan |last=Givony |date=July 17, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} As a freshman, he helped lead the Eagles to a 22–3 record and the semifinal of the prep national championship. As a sophomore, he averaged 10.0 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.2 assists while shooting 53.1 percent on 3-pointers, helping lead the Eagles to a perfect 25–0 record, and ranked No. 1 in the country, before the season was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2020/11/michigan-commit-caleb-houstan-scouting-report-one-of-best-shooters-in-country.html |title=Michigan commit Caleb Houstan scouting report: one of best shooters in country |website=MLive.com |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=November 4, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} Despite the season being cut short, Montverde was declared the prep national champions.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/11/13/mens-basketball-howard-signs-six-to-early-national-letters-of-intent.aspx |title=Howard Signs Six to Early National Letters of Intent |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |publisher=[[CBS Interactive]] |website=MGoBlue.com |date=November 13, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} He was the only non-senior to start on a roster with talented players such as [[Scottie Barnes]], [[Cade Cunningham]], [[Moses Moody]], [[Day'Ron Sharpe]], and Zeb Jackson.{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2020/10/30/five-star-caleb-houstan-no-8-2021-class-commits-michigan/6084259002/ |title=Five-star Caleb Houstan, No. 8 in 2021 class, commits to Michigan |newspaper=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=October 30, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} As a junior, he helped lead the Eagles to a 21–1 record, and the No. 1 seed in the inaugural NIBC tournament. Montverde Academy defeated Sunrise Christian Academy 61–57 to win the NIBC championship.{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/aFsTcZ4LxEmIZY9nKE7wNw/high-school-basketball--no-1-montverde-academy-defeats-no-3-sunrise-christian-academy-61-57-to-win-inaugural-nibc-championship.htm |title=High school basketball: No. 1 Montverde Academy defeats No. 3 Sunrise Christian Academy 61-57 to win inaugural NIBC championship |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |first=Jordan |last=Divens |date=March 12, 2021 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} On February 5, 2021, Sunrise Christian Academy defeated Montverde Academy 66–69 in overtime, ending high school basketball's longest win streak at 44 games. Houstan led Montverde with 19 points and 10 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/RXLoemkkIEe_x5xwzvZp3Q/high-school-basketball--no-3-sunrise-christian-academy-stuns-no-1-montverde-academy,-ends-44-game-win-streak.htm |title=High school basketball: No. 3 Sunrise Christian Academy stuns No. 1 Montverde Academy, ends 44-game win streak |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |first=Jordan |last=Divens |date=February 5, 2021 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} Houstan was named to the [[2021 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] rosters, becoming the first Michigan signee to earn the distinction since [[Daniel Horton (basketball)|Daniel Horton]] in [[2002 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2002]]. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and Jordan Brand Classic were not played for the second consecutive year.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2021/02/23/michigan-wolverines-mcdonalds-all-american-caleb-houstan-moussa-diabate-kobe-bufkin/4556432001/ |title=Michigan basketball breaks McDonald's All-American game drought |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Orion |last=Sang |date=February 23, 2021 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== On October 30, 2020, Houstan announced his commitment to playing college basketball for [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]]. He was the No. 2 rated player in the state of Florida, and was ranked the No. 14 overall prospect in the nation according to [[247Sports.com|247Sports]], and No. 4 power forward, becoming Michigan's highest-rated recruit in the modern recruiting era. Michigan's [[2021–22 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2021]] recruiting class is ranked No. 1 in the nation by 247Sports, [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2020/11/13/welcome-family-michigan-basketball-signs-top-ranked-recruiting-class/6279752002/ |title='Welcome to the family': Michigan basketball signs top-ranked recruiting class |newspaper=[[The Detroit News]] |first=James |last=Hawkins |date=November 13, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2021}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Caleb Houstan | position = [[Small forward|SF]] / [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Mississauga|Mississauga, Ontario]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = October 30, 2020 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2021 | rivals ref title = Michigan 2021 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2021 Michigan Wolverines Recruiting Class | rivals school = michigan | scout s = | espn schoolid = 130 | 247 overall = 14 | rivals overall = 8 | espn overall = 8 | accessdate = October 3, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On February 23, 2022, Houstan scored a career-high 21 points in a 71-62 win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]].{{cite news |title=Michigan's men's basketball team defeats Rutgers in 1st game under associate head coach Phil Martelli |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33357770/michigan-men-basketball-team-defeats-rutgers-1st-game-associate-head-coach-phil-martelli |access-date=February 24, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 23, 2022}} As a freshman, he averaged 10.1 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game. Following the season, Houstan declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite news |title=Houstan joins Diabate, declares for NBA Draft |first=Lindsay |last=Budin |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/sports/mens-basketball/houstan-joins-diabate-declares-for-nba-draft/ |newspaper=The Michigan Daily |publisher=michigandaily.com |date=April 25, 2022 |access-date=June 2, 2022}} However, on June 1, 2022, he announced that he would remain in the draft and forego his remaining eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Kahn |first1=Andrew |title=Michigan’s Caleb Houstan to stay in NBA draft|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2022/06/michigans-caleb-houstan-to-stay-in-nba-draft.html |access-date=June 1, 2022 |work=[[MLive.com]] |date=June 1, 2022}} ==National team career== Houstan represented [[Canada men's national under-17 basketball team|Canada]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in [[Belém]], Brazil. He started all six games and led Team Canada in scoring, and ranked second overall in the tournament, averaging 22.8 points while adding 5.3 rebounds, 2 assists and 1.7 steals, and helped his team win the silver medal. In the semifinals against [[Dominican Republic men's national under-16 basketball team|Dominican Republic]], Houstan led Canada with 29 points, breaking the record for most points in a game by a Canadian at the [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]].{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball.ca/news/caleb-houstan-named-to-mcdonalds-all-american-team |title=Caleb Houstan named to McDonald's All American team |website=basketball.ca |date=February 24, 2021 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} Following his outstanding performance, Houstan was named to the All-Star Five as well as All-Tournament team.{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/u16americas/2019/news/usa-claim-fiba-u16-americas-2019-title-in-belem |title=USA claim FIBA U16 Americas 2019 title in Belem |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=October 6, 2019 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} Houstan was scheduled to represent Canada at the [[2020 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2020 U17 World Cup]] and [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|U18 FIBA Americas Championship]], however, both events were postponed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/news/fibas-executive-committee-confirms-global-calendar-update |title=FIBA's Executive Committee confirms global calendar update |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=April 9, 2020 |access-date=March 22, 2021}} Houstan represented Canada at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], where he averaged 17 points, 5.7 rebounds, 2.4 assists, and 2.3 steals per game, to help lead his team to a bronze medal.{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/en/world/u19/2021/news/bediako-edey-houstan-mathurin-headline-star-studded-canadian-squad |title=Bediako, Edey, Houstan, Mathurin headline star-studded Canadian squad |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=June 30, 2021 |access-date=June 30, 2021}}{{cite
